zones.label: Day Shift Lab
zones.summary: In daylight the researcher watches three agents work, sees every action as it happens, and answers each request before the next step runs.
facts: Chapters 8 to 10 treated agents as tools you start, supervise, and stop. A session agent had the permissions you gave it for an afternoon (Chapter 19).
The remedies for a risky agent are least privilege, separate accounts or machines for separate risks, and approval for consequential actions (Chapter 19).
Begin new work at a low autonomy level from Chapter 9, and widen scope only on evidence (Chapter 19).
'Always-on' describes where the process runs and how long it lives, not how capable the model is (Chapter 19).

zones.label: Approval Requests
zones.summary: While you are present, requests arrive for your decision. An approval model sets which actions run alone, which are asked about, and which are blocked.
facts: The approval model is the policy that decides which actions the agent takes alone, which it asks about, and whether you can add your own rules (Chapter 19).
Some products document a permission layer that allows, blocks, or sends each action for approval. These are vendor-stated claims (Chapter 19).
To test an approval claim, create a harmless sensitive action and see whether the agent asks (Chapter 19).
In Chapter 19's illustrative audit, a purchase is out of scope because it leaves your control.

zones.label: Night Shift Lab
zones.summary: After dark the chair is empty, but a cloud computer glows teal. Agents read mail, run a sweep, file a ticket, and draft a summary with nobody watching.
facts: An always-on agent is a personal agent that continues to run when you are not present (Chapter 19).
A cloud agent computer sits in the vendor's data center with its own browser, files, and terminal, and keeps running when your computer is off (Chapter 19).
Delegated sign-in lets the agent log in to services as you, which means it holds the keys to your accounts (Chapter 19).
An always-on agent holds standing access to your accounts, remembers across weeks, and acts when nobody is looking (Chapter 19).

zones.label: Reach and Control
zones.summary: Three of the eight criteria: where the agent runs, how far its failure can spread, and which actions need a human.
facts: Where it runs: on your laptop, in the vendor's cloud, or on a server you manage. This decides where the computation and the data are (Chapter 19).
Blast radius is the extent of what an agent can read, change, or send if it is compromised, misdirected by injected text, or simply wrong (Chapter 19).
If all of a user's bots share one computer and one set of logins, the blast radius is everything that computer can reach (Chapter 19).
Approval model: which actions run alone, which are asked about, and whether you can add your own rules (Chapter 19).

zones.label: Cost and Data
zones.summary: Three more criteria: how usage is counted and capped, what happens to the data you give the agent, and what it remembers.
facts: Usage metering: ask how usage is counted, what the cap is, what happens at the cap, and whether you can see consumption as it accrues (Chapter 19).
Agentic work uses far more tokens than chat, and a routine that runs hourly multiplies it (Chapter 19).
Data exposure covers training use, retention, who can see the data, where it is processed, and whether memory can be inspected and deleted (Chapter 19).
Memory: keep the master knowledge graph where you control it, and treat what an agent writes into memory as a proposal you review (Chapter 19).

zones.label: Proof and Record
zones.summary: The last two criteria: whether anyone has tested the vendor's claims, and what record of last night's actions you will have in the morning.
facts: Claim verification: find the vendor's documentation for the claim, then test it hands-on with synthetic data and a throwaway account (Chapter 19).
Nearly all claims about these products are vendor-stated or from the press, and the research notes found no independent benchmarks or controlled tests (Chapter 19).
Activity audit: ask what record of last night's actions you will have in the morning (Chapter 19).
Prices, tiers, and features changed within weeks of launch, so the criteria outlast the product facts (Chapter 19).

zones.label: Morning Audit
zones.summary: Next morning the researcher reads the log against the task the agent was given and marks what was approved, what was unexpected, and what left their control.
facts: The overnight activity audit is the morning review of what the agent did while you were away (Chapter 19).
Its questions: what did it do, was each action within the task it was given, what did it spend, and did anything leave your control (Chapter 19).
An agent whose activity you cannot review is one you should not leave alone with anything that matters (Chapter 19).
In the illustrative log, reading one unrelated data file is out of scope even if it is harmless: scope, not apparent harm, is the test (Chapter 19).

quiz.question: A researcher watches three agents on screen, sees each action as it happens, and approves a step before it runs. Which region shows this?
quiz.explanation: A session agent works under your eyes with the permissions you gave it, so every action can be seen and stopped.

quiz.question: The lights are off and the chair is empty, yet a cloud computer reads email and runs a sweep using the researcher's sign-ins. Which region shows this?
quiz.explanation: An always-on agent keeps working on its own cloud computer with delegated sign-in while you are away.

quiz.question: Which region shows the policy that decides which actions an agent takes alone, which it asks about, and which it may not take?
quiz.explanation: This is the approval model, with approval requests reaching the researcher while they are present.

quiz.question: All of one user's bots share one computer and one set of logins, so one fooled bot acts with every credential. Which region shows the criteria that name this danger?
quiz.explanation: Blast radius and where the agent runs describe how far a single failure can spread.

quiz.question: An hourly routine will run all week, and you also want to know whether your inputs are used for training. Which region shows the criteria to check?
quiz.explanation: Usage metering covers how consumption is counted and capped, and data exposure covers training use and retention.

quiz.question: A vendor says the agent always asks before sensitive actions, and no outsider has tested it. Which region shows how to treat that claim?
quiz.explanation: Claim verification means testing the claim yourself with synthetic data and a throwaway account, and the activity record is how you check what happened.

quiz.question: At 8 a.m. you compare each logged action with the task the agent was given. Which region shows this routine?
quiz.explanation: The overnight activity audit checks each action against the task, what was spent, and whether anything left your control.

quiz.question: An agent read one data file that was not part of its task. It looked harmless. Which region shows where that is judged?
quiz.explanation: Scope is the test, not apparent harm, so reading any file outside the allowed list counts as out of scope.

quiz.question: The research notes found no independent benchmarks of these products, only vendor statements. Which region shows what to do about that?
quiz.explanation: Without independent evidence, you verify the claims that matter yourself and keep a record you can review.
